title: Hyperlane scheduler misprioritization causing tokens/sec sag across deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported a sudden tokens/sec degradation and increased TTFT on 2026-03-11. The impact was visible in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; symptoms included slow initial token emission (TTFT up ~50-120ms) and sustained tokens/sec drop (~30-45%) for long-context and sparse-attention model families. This ticket tracks triage, immediate mitigation, hotfix rollout, and follow-ups.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC - Pager alert: global tokens/sec aggregated metric dropped 35% vs baseline. SRE alerted on-call.
2026-03-11 03:22 UTC - Customer AcmeDocs opened escalation citing production latency regressions impacting ingestion pipeline. Channel #inc-acme-acmedocs created.
2026-03-11 03:40 UTC - Initial triage found correlation with runtime change merged 2026-03-10 (scheduler heuristics for kernel selection).
2026-03-11 04:15 UTC - Reproduced tokens/sec sag locally using long-context benchmark with sparse-attn model; profiler shows increased eviction/warmup cycles and KV cache misses during priming.
2026-03-11 04:55 UTC - Implemented emergency hotfix: force legacy scheduler path for affected model families and enable prefetch backoff. Deployed to canary pool.
2026-03-11 06:10 UTC - Canary metrics recovered (tokens/sec within 5% of baseline). Gradual rollout to hosted fleet and dedicated pools started.
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC - Private customer air-gapped packages prepared and patch notes delivered to SE for on-prem installs.
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Postmortem draft created and follow-up items assigned. Ticket marked Done after verification window.
mitigation_steps: Immediate rollback path: for Hosted/Dedicated we flipped scheduler flag to legacy-mode and throttled prefetching (deployed 2026-03-11 04:55 UTC, deploy id deploy-2026-03-11-07a).
Canary validation: ran long-context and streaming benchmarks (50k requests) with customer-like prompt shapes before wider rollout.
Private customers: provided patch bundle and upgrade instructions; coordinated with SE to schedule non-disruptive upgrade windows.
Communications: customer-facing incident summary sent to affected accounts and internal summary posted to #incidents and #runtime.
root_cause: A change to the Hyperlane scheduler heuristics (commit abcdef12 merged 2026-03-10) caused the kernel-selection score to prefer an int8 execution path that interacts poorly with the runtime's KV-prefetch timing for sparse-attention families. The new path increased eviction frequency of priming prefixes and forced repeated warmup kernel loads, causing higher TTFT and sustained tokens/sec degradation under typical multi-tenant fanout.
regressions_identified: Scheduler kernel-scoring became sensitive to short-lived queue spikes and over-indexed on estimated throughput instead of priming retention.
Prefetch aggressiveness did not account for heterogeneous model stride; this caused unnecessary weight streaming and cache churn.
Fallback selector did not trigger quickly enough because failure thresholds were tuned for throughput-only regressions, not warmup churn.

next_steps: Rework scheduler scoring to include priming retention score and a penalty for excessive KV eviction (owner: Marco DeLuca, due 2026-03-25).
Add e2e benchmark that simulates multi-tenant long-context priming across sparse-attn and dense families; include in CI (owner: Sofia Nguyen, estimate 5).
Tune fallback thresholds to detect warmup churn faster and fall back to legacy scheduler within 200ms of TTFT regression (owner: Ethan Kim).
Post-deploy monitor: add automated regression alert that watches per-model-family tokens/sec abnormal drop for 15m windows.
